newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sarasin H1 profit up, outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Sarasin H1 profit up, outlook positive.

text.p: Bank Sarasin & Co said its consolidated profit in the first half of 1997 to the end of June rose 58.5 percent, and that its outlook for the remainder of the year was favourable.
"Based on current market expectations, we believe that the coming months should bring sucess," Sarasin said.
But it added: "Because the environment so far has been above expectations, a consolidation in the second half is more probable than an unlimited continuation (of the current trend)."
Consolidated profits in the first half rose to 28.45 million Swiss francs from 17.95 million in the first half of 1996, Sarasin said.
It said the main increases came from higher commission earnings and favourable trading results.
Cash flow at Sarasin reached 39.1 million francs, an increase of 11.4 million francs or 41 percent compared with the first half of 1996.

Assets rose to 2.408 billion Swiss francs in the first half from 1.785 billion at the end of 1996, an increase of 623 million francs or 34.9 percent. Nearly 380 million francs of the increase was tied to new inflows of customer money.
Bank Sarasin, with eight partners, is considered to be one of Switzerland's top four strictly private banks.
